challenges.expected_behavior: Make the gate capability-rooted rather than member-name-rooted. Track any ast.Attribute whose attr is a capability export name (json, sys, builtins, importlib, os) as binding that capability regardless of the receiver, register the resulting expression in semantic_modules, and then apply the existing json member policy to it - so parser.json.<anything> is a violation unless it is dumps in a direct call, or loads in the canonical parser or the documented offline allowance. Add the transported-JSONDecoder, transported-decoder-submodule, raw_decode, scan_once and hoisted-class forms to the committed rejection census in test_direct_parser_policy_rejects_representation_independent_bypasses, and add an assertion that the closure contains no reference to any json-module member outside the two authorized sites.
challenges.observed_behavior: All ten accepted. check_f017_bounded_artifact_decode_policy_v1.validate() returned result=PASS, violations=[], runtime_import_closure_count=32, and its direct_decode_sites census still listed only the two authorized sites - the planted decoder was not enumerated. Root cause: the repair's two new helpers, _name_agnostic_decode_sites and _name_agnostic_decode_member_escapes, both filter on node.attr in {'load','loads'}, and the attribute name 'json' is absent from DYNAMIC_CAPABILITY_ATTRIBUTES, so an ast.Attribute chain rooted at a first-party module name reaches the genuine json module through a name the policy never tracks. CAPABILITY_REEXPORT_IMPORT closes only the ImportFrom spelling, not the attribute-access spelling. The planted decoders then performed genuinely unbounded decodes: raw RecursionError escaped the canonical boundary at nesting depth 100000, duplicate keys silently collapsed to {'a': 2}, NaN and Infinity were accepted, noncanonical spacing and ordering were accepted, a 5 MB string was accepted, and a non-dict top level was accepted - every one of which the canonical parser rejects as ArtifactDecodeError on the identical bytes. This falsifies the frozen contract clause direct_active_runtime_json_load_or_loads=PROHIBITED_OUTSIDE_CANONICAL_PARSER and is the same defect class as cycle-02 O-C02-001, one representation removed. The defect is latent, not active: an independent census found zero such constructs in the committed closure.

More durably, land the capability-rooted rewrite in O-C03-001, which removes the receiver parser.json from reach and makes the operator-module route unconstructible.
challenges.observed_behavior: All three accepted with result=PASS and violations=[]. The policy rejects getattr, setattr, vars, globals, locals, eval, exec, compile, __import__, __dict__, __getattribute__ and sys.modules, and the repair added 'load'/'loads' to the getattr member check, but there is no rule for the operator module, so attrgetter and methodcaller retrieve the identical bound method with the capability name appearing only as a plain string constant the policy never inspects. Verified end-to-end: the attrgetter and methodcaller forms both collapsed duplicate keys to {'a': 2} and accepted NaN, and accepted nesting depth 100000 that the canonical parser rejects. Note that operator.itemgetter('loads')(parser.json.__dict__) IS correctly rejected, but only incidentally, by the pre-existing __dict__ rule - not by any name-agnostic reasoning about the retrieved member.
